html:
Working example of the Essay template (the Fonio layout: big section headings, side notes in the margin, section menu pill at the bottom). It shows every building block from the Style Guide. See it at adjoakittoe.com/#example-essay↗. Each gray line explains the block right under it. To start your own: ••• (top right) → Duplicate → rename it, change the Slug, delete the gray lines and this box.

Text before the first Heading 1 is the opening. It has no section name.

This opening paragraph has a side note in the margin. Fonio has been grown in West Africa for thousands of years.1

a This is a side note. Make one by clicking at the end of a paragraph or list item, pressing Enter, pressing Tab (it tucks under the line above), then typing /callout.

Text

Heading 1 (/h1) starts a section. Its name goes in the section menu pill. Heading 2 (/h2) and Heading 3 (/h3) are smaller headings inside a section.

A Heading 2

A Heading 3

Body text with bold, italic, struck, a highlight, muted words, a key like ⌘ + K, a Tag, and inline code.

Bold, italic, struck: select words → B, i, S in the toolbar. Highlight: A (color) → Background → Yellow. Muted: A → Text → Gray. Tag: A → Background → Gray. Key: inline code with 1 to 3 characters (select → click the <> button). Longer inline code stays code.

Links

Dotted link leaving the site, with ↗: select words → Link → paste a web address.

Read more from the Whole Grains Council↗.

Internal link with →: type @ and pick a page from Essays & Vibe Projects.

See EXAMPLE: Recipe → for the recipe layout.

Green in-text link (used rarely, inside a sentence): select words → Link → search and pick a page from Essays & Vibe Projects.

This sentence has a green link to the recipe inside it.

Jump down the page with ↓: right-click a heading → Copy link to block. Then select words → Link → paste.

Button: a line that is only a bold link.

Open the recipe

Download button: /file → Upload a PDF. The caption is the button text.

Download the sample PDF

Citations

Type [1] right after a sentence. For two sources type [1, 2]. Hover the number on the site to see the source pop up. The sources themselves go in the Sources section at the end.

One cup of dry fonio makes about four cups cooked.1,2

Lists

Bullets: - and a space. Press Tab on a new line to nest one.

  • Unordered item
  • With a nested list
    • Nested item
  • Last item

Numbers: 1. and a space.

  1. Ordered item
  2. Second
  3. Third

Numbered step with a badge: a numbered list where every item starts with bold words. The bold words become the step heading.

1

Rinse the grain.

Cover it with water and swirl.

2

Toast it.

Two minutes in a little oil.

Glossary: bullets where every item starts with a bold word and a colon.

Fonio
a tiny, fast-cooking grain.
Teff
the grain used to make injera.

Quotes

Block quote: type " and a space. Who said it: Shift+Enter inside the quote, then ~ and the name.

Someone else's words go here.Source name

Pull quote (larger): start the quote with a quotation mark.

"A line worth stopping on."Bee

Note box: /callout with any icon except the special ones below.

Note. A callout box for a tip, warning, or aside.

Code

/code makes a code box with a Copy code button under it.

const fonio = { cups: 1, cooked: 4, minutes: 5 };

Tables

Table with a header: /table → click the table → ••• → turn on Header row. Put a bold-only line right above it to give it a title.

Table with a header
GrainCook timeYield
Fonio5 min1 → 4 cups

Facts table (also called a catalog entry): Header row off, two columns. Labels sit on the left.

Catalog entry

Hover rows (rows tint when hovered): ••• → turn on Header column instead of Header row.

Hover rows
Row oneRows tint when you hover them.
Row twoUseful for scannable lists.

Images

/image → Upload. Click under the photo to write the caption. Every photo opens bigger when clicked. Add a credit after a | in the caption. Shapes: end the caption with (square), (round), (circle), or (wide) for edge to edge, or (tilt) for a photo that tilts on hover.

Side by side: drag one image next to another until a blue line appears.

Slideshow, gallery, tabs

Slideshow with ‹ › arrows: /toggle named exactly Slideshow with images inside. Each caption shows under the slides.

  1. First slide caption.
  2. Second slide caption.
  3. Third slide caption.

Gallery grid: /toggle named exactly Gallery with images inside.

Tabs: /toggle named exactly Tabs. Inside it, one toggle per tab: its name is the tab label, what's inside is the tab.

Tabbed content, one panel at a time.

The second panel.

Accordion: /toggle with any other name.

An accordion: click to open

Hidden content that expands in place.

Year accordion (like Now): /toggle named with just a year, with bullets inside. The count of updates is added for you.

  • First update
  • Second update
  • Third update

Data

Big stats: /callout with the 📊 icon. One per line (Shift+Enter): bold number first, then the label.

+82% A big stat with a label
45+ Another stat
3 A third

Progress bars: /callout with the 📈 icon. One per line: a label, then a percent.

Progress62%
Tarot deck13%

Color swatches: /callout with the 🎨 icon and hex codes.

Woven stripe (for special moments): /callout with the 🧵 icon, nothing inside.

Timeline

/toggle named exactly Timeline. Inside it a table with Header row on and three columns: Year, Title, Detail. Click a year or use the arrows.

1929. Each point opens a short note below.

1991. Use the arrows, tap a year, or scroll sideways.

2026. Notes can hold a sentence or two.

Archival pieces

Specimen card: /toggle named Specimen: and a number. Inside: one image and a two-column table (no header). Put several Specimen toggles in a row and they sit side by side.

Media

Photo on hover: color the word purple (A → Text → Purple), then add a row with the same word in Hover Images. The row named fonio is set up for this one.

This is a sentence about fonio with a photo on hover.

Video that plays in the middle of the screen: /video → Embed link → paste a YouTube or Vimeo address.

Audio player: /audio → Upload an audio file. The caption is the track name.

Link card: paste a web address on an empty line → choose Create bookmark.

Divider: type --- (three dashes).

Sources

title: EXAMPLE: Recipe
dek: The one or two sentences under the title go in the Dek property at the top of this row.
html:
Working example of the Recipe template (same layout as Curried Fonio Pilaf). See it at adjoakittoe.com/#example-recipe↗. The section menu on the right is made from your Heading 1s. Side notes sit in the margin. To start your own: ••• (top right) → Duplicate → rename it, change the Slug, delete the gray lines and this box.

Headnote

Every Heading 1 becomes a section and a link in the side menu. Ingredients, Method, and Notes get their colors automatically.

A five-minute grain and a ten-minute pilaf. Onion and ginger do most of the work.1

a Side note in the margin. Make one: click at the end of the paragraph or step, press Enter, press Tab, type /callout. Side notes get letters a, b, c for you.

Ingredients

Heading 1 named exactly Ingredients, then bullets. Start each with an amount and a unit (cup, tbsp, tsp, g, oz, can, clove, small, pinch). The Serves buttons (from the Serves property) multiply the amounts. A line with no amount is left as is.

Serves
  • ½ cup fonio
  • 1 tbsp oil, for coating the fonio
  • 1 cup water
  • ½ tsp salt
  • 1 small onion, diced
  • Herbs and a lime, to finish

Method

Heading 1 named exactly Method, then a numbered list. Start each step with bold words.

  1. Cook the fonio. Coat the fonio with the oil, add the water and salt, cover, and cook on low about 5 minutes.1
  2. Build the base. Sauté the onion in a large pan for 3 to 5 minutes.
  3. Fold. Fold in the fonio and turn off the heat.

b Soggy? Cook off the remaining liquid. Dry? Add a spoonful of water.

To serve

Finish with herbs and a squeeze of lime.

Notes

Heading 1 named exactly Notes, then bullets.

  • Fonio is forgiving, so small changes in water are fine.
  • Make it a bowl with roasted vegetables.

Sources

  1. 1
    Yolélé Fonio, product packaging ↗ Brand
    Cooking time and yield, as printed on the bag.

Anything before the first Heading 1 shows at the top of the right column.

The recipes

dek: Mapping the invisible calendar that governs food systems, not just climate seasons, but the deeper rhythms of soil, water, labor, and harvest cycles.
